---
title: "Empirical Study Results"
date: "2026-4-30"
image: slides/AppImage.png
---

The empirical study for my project focused on benchmarking performance as the dataset size increased. I tested loading, querying, 
and chart rendering using workout datasets containing 100, 1,000, and 10,000 entries. The results showed that most operations 
remained highly responsive even at larger scales, especially when limiting chart rendering to recent data points. One interesting 
result was that the first benchmark run was often slower due to initialization overhead, while later runs stabilized significantly.
Overall, the study demonstrated that the application’s architecture and data management approach were efficient enough to support 
realistic long-term usage.

The study also reinforced the importance of experimental evaluation in software development. Rather than assuming the application 
would perform well, the benchmarking process provided measurable evidence about how the system behaved under different workloads. 
It also highlighted areas where optimization mattered most, such as reducing unnecessary rendering and improving data filtering 
efficiency. Conducting these experiments helped connect the technical implementation of the project to broader concepts in 
computer science, including performance analysis, scalability, and system reliability.
